members_read: Palace development/Loudon Live Design System.md (frontmatter only, for verification)
summary: This room is an odd pairing — three palace-governance foundationals (CLAUDE, ELDER, SCHEMA — Reference) sitting beside five Shop visualization/document Specialists (D3.js, Observable Plot, Matplotlib, Mermaid, LaTeX) — and it turned out to hold two genuinely different kinds of find. The first is structural: ELDER and CLAUDE each name a known entry in their own body prose (Agent Toolbox, Loudon Live Design System) that governs exactly the kind of work the Specialists in this room do, but neither carries the frontmatter link — both are on the under-reached newcomer list, so wiring them is a real, low-risk gain. The second is more interesting: the five Specialists all independently reach for the same unmet need — a house-palette wrapper so Loudon Live tokens survive a skin swap — and two of them (D3.js, Observable Plot) already solved it with the same idiom (read design tokens at render/call time, never at module load), while Matplotlib, Mermaid, and (eventually) LaTeX are each about to reinvent it from zero. Matplotlib's own forward_vector even names Observable Plot's wrapper as the model to follow, in words, without a link. Nothing here needed a force — the Specialists are healthy, sharply differentiated by charter, and their "Lost Branches" sections show they already turned down easy mergers (Chart.js, D2, Typst) for the right reasons, so this room has no compost or merge candidates, only a couple of missing wires and one open question (D3.js's "defer to the Plot Specialist when it exists") that the room itself has already answered.

open_question_resolutions.proposed_action: Retire or rewrite this line — Observable Plot (the 'Plot Specialist') is now alive and shipped its own wrapper (palace-plot-defaults.js), and D3.js separately grew its own § Working within the Loudon Live design system that reads palaceTokens() directly at render/tick time. The two solved this independently rather than one deferring to the other; the open question predates both solutions and no longer describes the current state.

coherence_findings.issue: Two Shop Specialists (D3.js, Observable Plot) independently solved the same problem — a house-palette wrapper that reads Loudon Live design tokens at render/call time so a skin swap propagates without stale hex literals — and documented it as a named pattern. Three siblings (Matplotlib's palace.mplstyle, Mermaid's --cssFile wrapper, LaTeX's palace.sty) each carry an open forward_vector / Open Questions item asking for the same thing, none cross-referencing the two that already exist.
coherence_findings.proposed_action: When Matplotlib, Mermaid, or LaTeX takes its first house-styled job, point the wrapper build at D3.js's § Working within the Loudon Live design system and Observable Plot's palace-plot-defaults.js as the worked pattern rather than reinventing from zero. The Matplotlib→Observable Plot link proposed above is the first concrete step; Mermaid and LaTeX could take the analogous connects-to once their own wrapper work starts (not proposed here — no body-text evidence yet, would be forcing it).

synthesis_spawn_flag.unnamed_idea: Token-read-at-call-time as the house integration pattern for Shop visual Specialists
synthesis_spawn_flag.why_load_bearing: D3.js and Observable Plot each independently arrived at the same idiom — read Loudon Live design tokens inside render()/call time rather than at module load, so a live skin swap re-colors output without a stale-hex risk — and both wrote it up under near-identical section headers. Matplotlib, Mermaid, and (eventually) LaTeX are each reaching for the same capability separately. A small named pattern note would let the next three specialists build it once instead of three more times from scratch.
